correctness.rationale: The Procházka--Rueda Zoca characterization reduces octahedrality to the long trapezoid property. If \(c\le b\), choosing two fresh points \(x_i,x_j\) gives the LTP inequalities exactly for every finite test set; the only nontrivial cases reduce to \(c\le b\) and \(a\le2b\). If \(c>b\), exhaustive pair-type reduction for the test set \(\{o,z\}\) gives the exact supremum \(\max\{(a+b)/(a+c),a/(b+c)\}\), and both terms are strictly below one under the metric constraints. The repository pair-type checker verifies the finite case split over many exact rational triples, but the symbolic case reduction is the proof.
correctness.risk: The formula is specific to this homogeneous countable metric family and the standard basepoint convention.

value.rationale: The family is the natural three-distance deformation of a canonical counterexample in the foundational paper, and the result turns one isolated example into a complete sharp phase diagram with an exact obstruction constant. This is a motivated structural classification.

final_claim: For the metric family \(M(a,b,c)=\{o,z\}\cup\{x_n:n\in\mathbb N\}\) with \(d(o,x_n)=d(x_n,x_m)=a\), \(d(z,x_n)=b\), and \(d(o,z)=c\), subject to the metric inequalities, \(\mathcal F(M(a,b,c))\) has an octahedral norm exactly when \(c\le b\); when \(c>b\), the exact two-point long-trapezoid obstruction ratio for \(\{o,z\}\) is \(\max\{(a+b)/(a+c),a/(b+c)\}\).
limitations: No claim is made for arbitrary bounded uniformly discrete metric spaces.
